newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed lower on Thursday amid a flurry of last-minute profit-taking by speculators coupled with absence of buying by financial institutions, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 7.40 points lower at 704.85.
"Share prices failed to sustain yesterday's gains as profit- taking by speculators disrupted the rally," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.

Delhi share index had jumped 3.3 percent on Wednesday after Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday that government planned by mid-January to announce moves to boost industrial production and revive capital markets.
"It was a technical correction as the prices had zoomed up suddenly," said another broker.
Reliance Industries dropped 4.10 rupees to 214 on sustained selling by speculators, brokers said.
TISCO fell 1.90 rupees to 180.05 following a late burst of profit-taking by speculators.
ITC, in line with general trend, slipped 3.80 rupees to 337.10.
Larsen and Toubro shed 4.95 rupees to 228.25.
